page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the n2d family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, containing 1 physical core with 2 threads. The system is configured with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache specifications include 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the top 25% at 2684.89. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show limitations. Stress-ng multi-core performance falls in the bottom 25%, and Passmark CPU scores are similarly positioned. Memory bandwidth is constrained, with read-only small block cached bandwidth scoring in the bottom 10% at 125.99 GB/sec, and large block uncached read/write speeds registering in the bottom 25%. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, achieve average tier performance. Conversely, database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput fall into the bottom 10% of benchmarked systems.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-highcpu-2 offers a low-resource entry point within the dedicated AMD EPYC hardware class, trading off memory capacity and multi-core throughput for dedicated single-core execution. The low RAM-to-vCPU ratio makes it less suitable for memory-intensive databases, software compilation, or complex rendering tasks, which score in the bottom 10% on Geekbench. It is best utilized for lightweight, single-threaded compute tasks, basic text processing, and low-throughput web serving workloads that do not require significant memory footprints or local storage.
